userStories.title: E2E contract rewrite + pure tool-presentation policy
userStories.description: As an operator scanning agent-node transcripts, I want a single deterministic React-free presentation policy that resolves any stored tool call into family, chip label, headline, status, and ordered badges, with the stale visible-JSON E2E expectations first rewritten to the new collapsed-row contract, so that both surfaces can render identical meaning without exposing serialized data.
acceptanceCriteria: TDD order: the three obsolete E2E cases are rewritten FIRST and confirmed failing against the old .ptool card UI for the intended reason — e2e/ui/workflow-run-hitl.spec.ts '[V:hitl.console-tool-output]' (:79) and '[V:hitl.legacy-tool-output]' (:94), and '[V:hitl.agent-history]' in e2e/ui/workflow-run-hitl-room.spec.ts (:208, assertions :219-223)

Rewritten cases target `details[data-tool-id] > summary`, assert the success row is closed, verify chip/headline text, and assert Input/Output/payload output are not visible; titles keep uppercase 'HITL' and include 'readable tool row' so `--grep "HITL.*readable tool row"` selects them

New packages/web/src/lib/tool-presentation.ts is React-free, fully typed (no `any`), exports `toolPresentation(input)` and `toolRowPresentation(input, facts)`; `ToolPresentationInput` is exactly `{name, input, output}` and does not depend on AgentHistoryItem

Nine families resolve correctly: shell|file|search|glob|code|todo|task|web|generic via the exact normalized alias table in phase-01-start.md; case-fold + strip `_`/`-` normalization; substring matching forbidden (`search_replace` → file, never search)

Resolution precedence: bounded `mcp__server__tool` → generic with `server · tool` display (input keys cannot reclassify); exact alias; known-input-key inference in contract priority; Codex name-only shell path for absent/empty input with command-like or overlong multiline name; else generic

Family headline rules implemented per plan: shell command/cmd/script + complete `/bin/zsh -lc` or `/bin/bash -lc` wrapper strip + `…` for later lines; file path keys; search pattern+scope; glob pattern/path inversion; code first line + language badge; todo `todo updated` + bounded `op:` badge; task description/name/context order; web URL; generic ≤3 scalar `key: value` facts with NO `{…}`/`[n]` serialization markers in the collapsed headline
Chip shows exact sent name only when a bounded scan proves one whitespace-free token ≤24 Unicode code points; otherwise the family label; rejected names never leak into accessibility text

All named bounds enforced with limit and limit+1 tests: MAX_ALIAS_NAME_CODE_UNITS=128, MAX_CHIP_CODE_POINTS=24, MAX_HEADLINE_SOURCE_CODE_UNITS=4096 (over-cap → safe fallback, never a fabricated partial path), MAX_GENERIC_KEYS_SCANNED=32, MAX_GENERIC_FACTS=3, MAX_GENERIC_SCALAR_CODE_POINTS=80, MAX_COUNT_OUTPUT_CODE_UNITS=4096, MAX_COUNT_KEYS_SCANNED=32

Badge order deterministic: visible running/interrupted state → content fact (language/count/operation) → exit → non-full output-state → duration last; running = `running · <elapsed>` suppressing premature `missing`; interrupted = `interrupted`; unknown = `output unknown`; settled rows keep recorded truncated/missing/unknown marker; no facts → `—` placeholder; count only from bounded scalar/shallow exact count fields, omitted on unsupported shapes
Public `toolPresentation` catches unexpected failure and returns a safe generic row while `toolRowPresentation` still preserves derived outcome glyph and operational facts
Nulls, arrays, deeply nested/wide objects, huge strings, unknown metadata cannot throw or trigger unbounded traversal — covered by adversarial unit tests
`bun test src/lib/tool-presentation.test.ts` passes from packages/web and `bun run type-check` is clean; the three E2E cases remain red (renderers have not moved yet)
userStories.technicalNotes: Follow plans/260917-1011-issue-174-readable-tool-call-row/phase-01-start.md (Row model, Resolver and headline rules, Explicit bounds, Tests before production code). Reuse formatDurationMs/ensureUtc from packages/web/src/lib/format.ts:28,:2. pair-tool-transcript.ts is read-only. Duration badge formatting must come from lib/format.ts, not a new helper.
userStories.notes: Implemented in iteration 1. Files: e2e/ui/workflow-run-hitl.spec.ts, e2e/ui/workflow-run-hitl-room.spec.ts (3 HITL cases rewritten to details[data-tool-id] > summary, confirmed red on old .ptool UI), packages/web/src/lib/tool-presentation.ts, packages/web/src/lib/tool-presentation.test.ts (141 tests).

userStories.title: History projection: exit code, presentation, interruption fold, render clock
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the shared buildAgentHistory projection to carry exit codes, a ready-made row presentation, deterministic running elapsed time, and the adjacent-interruption override, so that every mounted transcript surface shows the same truthful tool row.
acceptanceCriteria: AgentHistoryInput (packages/web/src/lib/agent-history.ts:12) gains required `nowMs: number`; the AgentHistoryItem tool arm (:26-41) gains `exitCode: number | null` and `presentation: ToolRowPresentation` while keeping name/input/output/outcome/durationMs/canLoadFullOutput/outputState/messageId/toolUseId/id/seq — `context` is retained until US-004

Exit code is extracted once with existing precedence (result metadata → call metadata → paired card, see extraToolFields :104 and deriveOutcome :120) and shared between outcome derivation and the presenter

Completed duration keeps the exact single-match `tool_completed.data.duration_ms` behavior in toolRuntime (:185); running elapsed uses the one exact matching `tool_called` event's created_at parsed via ensureUtc plus `max(0, nowMs - startedAt)`; invalid, missing, or ambiguous starts produce NO elapsed badge

Adjacent interruption fold implemented as a single ordered look-ahead in buildAgentHistory (:207): a tool card immediately followed by a status message whose state is exactly `interrupted` projects the tool with outcome `interrupted`, recomputes its presentation, consumes that one status row, and advances; no fold on detail text, substring matches, other states, or across any intervening item; the override beats failed metadata/exit code for display while the exit badge may remain a fact; direct-result `interrupted` still works

All three production callers hoist and pass their existing per-render Date.now() snapshot — NodeTranscriptPane.tsx:236 (move the :284 nowMs above the call), ConsoleNodeRoom.tsx:607 (:652), ConsoleExecutionHistory.tsx:204 (:217) — so Ask cards and tool rows share one render clock; no new interval, timer, or lifecycle mutation is added
buildAgentHistory keeps returning AgentHistoryItem[] and all existing consumers still type-check

Projection unit tests cover exit precedence, completed duration, deterministic running elapsed, missing/ambiguous/invalid start, direct and adjacent interruption (including failed-plus-interrupted), stable order and IDs: `bun test src/lib/agent-history.test.ts src/lib/pair-tool-transcript.test.ts` passes and `bun run type-check` is clean from packages/web
The three rewritten HITL E2E cases remain red only because renderers have not moved yet (verified via the --grep "HITL.*readable tool row" selector)
userStories.technicalNotes: Follow phase-01-start.md sections 'Outcome, exit code, and interruption' and 'Row model' (nowMs contract). toToolItem (:146) is where presentation attaches. Do not remove `context`/`toolContext`/`TOOL_CONTEXT_KEYS` yet — renderers still read them until US-004.
userStories.notes: Implemented in iteration 2. Files: packages/web/src/lib/agent-history.ts (nowMs input, exitCode + presentation on tool arm, toolExitCode/toolStartedAtMs/runningElapsed helpers, adjacent interrupted fold), agent-history.test.ts (19 tests), NodeTranscriptPane/ConsoleNodeRoom/ConsoleExecutionHistory (hoisted per-render nowMs), NodeRoom.test.tsx fixture.

userStories.title: Legacy NodeRoom native disclosure row
userStories.description: As an operator in the Legacy node room, I want each tool call rendered as one compact native <details> row with stable operator-controlled disclosure state, so that I can scan outcomes at a glance and expand diagnostics deliberately.
acceptanceCriteria: Component tests updated FIRST and confirmed red: packages/web/src/components/workflows/NodeRoom.test.tsx (static DOM/anatomy/diagnostics) and LegacyNodeRoom.test.tsx (interactive rerender, pointer, keyboard, focus, loading)

Each tool item renders one `<details data-tool-id={item.toolUseId}>` keyed by the existing stable item id; direct `<summary>` contains in accessible-name order: aria-hidden chevron, visually-hidden status word + aria-hidden glyph (✓/✕/◐/⚠/–), chip with `family · displayed-label` title (family only when identical), headline, ordered badge group with decorative separators; visible running/interrupted badge texts and the `—` placeholder are aria-hidden

Disclosure state algorithm: `open` initializes from `presentation.initialOpen` only on mount/item-identity change; pointer AND Enter/Space toggles mark the row touched; an untouched row becoming failed opens once; no path ever auto-closes; programmatic controlled-open toggles are not mistaken for user action; nested diagnostic toggles are ignored via `event.target !== event.currentTarget`; new item identity resets to its own initial policy

Opened body starts with a minimal bar whose first word is the family followed by every summary fact including duration; nested Input/Output remain closed <details> styled as real controls (text-secondary, ≥24 px target, visible accent focus, native Enter/Space, DOM/Tab order after the outer summary); a failed auto-opened row still exposes no serialized payload until a diagnostic is opened

Existing full-output control, loading, error, and retry semantics are preserved below the diagnostics (not moved into the summary); after a successful local load the shell re-runs `toolRowPresentation` with unchanged facts + loaded output + `outputState: 'full'`, removing a stale `truncated` badge without resetting disclosure state or the item key

Legacy visual contract: rest transparent on room surface (no .ptool inset card fill/border/shadow), hover surface-hover, focus 2 px --accent-bright outline with −2 px offset; transcript padding 10 px/12 px; no inherited 12 px gap between adjacent collapsed tool rows while assistant/lifecycle/extension content keeps explicit per-item separation

Row geometry: summary 12 px mono weight 400, 4/6 padding, 8 gap, 6 radius, ≥24 px height, single line; chevron 10 px text in fixed 9 px column, 90° open rotation over 120 ms with motion-reduce disabling the transition; glyph 12 px bold centered in fixed 12 px column; only the glyph is bold

Chip 11 px mono, 1/7 padding, 4 radius, ≤24ch, surface-elevated with family border/text tones (shell/code=bash, file/web=command, search/glob=prompt via `color-mix(in oklch, var(--node-prompt) 70%, var(--text-primary))` text and documented 45% border mix, todo/task=approval, generic=secondary)

Path-kind headlines split into a shrinkable secondary head and fixed primary tail preserving the final nonempty segment for `/` and `\` separators and URLs (trailing separators kept with tail, tail capped at 100% of wrapper with ellipsis); text-kind headlines use one end-ellipsis span; the full accepted string stays in the DOM

Badges 11 px mono secondary right-aligned non-wrapping; duration carries `flex: 0 1 auto` + min-width 0 so it drops first; nonzero exit digits use a token-derived error/primary mix; body margin 2/0/8/29 with 2 px token rail and 10 px left padding, 10.5 px mono secondary text

Full test matrix green in both Legacy test files: five initial outcomes → closed/open/closed/closed/closed with exact glyph+hidden word; pointer and keyboard toggles survive rerenders/polling; untouched →failed opens once; touched rows never overridden; identity reset; accessible-name order; path/URL/text elision anatomy; width priority; body bar facts; diagnostics defaults/isolation/accessibility; extension-slot anchoring; focus stability on append; adjacent-row rhythm; queries scoped to the direct summary (no host textContent treating hidden payload as visible)

Verification passes from packages/web: `NODE_ENV=development bun test src/components/workflows/NodeRoom.test.tsx`, `NODE_ENV=development bun test src/components/workflows/LegacyNodeRoom.test.tsx`, `bun test src/lib/agent-history.test.ts`, `bun run type-check`; HITL E2E green is NOT required here (lands in US-004)
userStories.technicalNotes: Follow phase-02-two-surface-renderers.md sections 'Required DOM and interaction contract', 'Disclosure state algorithm', 'Visual implementation contract'. Legacy owns tool markup in NodeRoom.tsx:227/.ptool card and :246 item.context — replace with item.presentation. Use existing token-backed utilities plus small typed local class/style maps; no new tokens, stylesheet, shared component, or shared hook.

userStories.title: Console history row + context cleanup + HITL E2E green
userStories.description: As an operator in the Console, I want the same disclosure-row semantics in both the selected-room history and the inline execution history, so that one stored tool call means the same thing on every surface.
acceptanceCriteria: Component tests updated FIRST and confirmed red: packages/web/src/experiments/console/components/ConsoleNodeRoom.test.tsx (selected-room anatomy/interactions) and inspect/ConsoleExecutionHistory.test.tsx (inline-history reuse/regression)

ConsoleAgentHistoryList.tsx implements the identical semantic anatomy and disclosure-state transition matrix as Legacy (details[data-tool-id] > summary, chevron/hidden-word/glyph/chip/headline/badges, touched/untouched rules, nested-toggle isolation, identity reset) WITHOUT importing any Legacy component — small intentional JSX duplication is acceptable; if the logic cannot stay identical, pause rather than introducing a shared React component or hook
Console-specific deltas applied: focus outline offset is +2 px (vs Legacy −2 px); running badge uses the Console --running token; all other geometry/typography/badge/body rules identical to US-003
Both Console mounts verified: ConsoleNodeRoom selected-room history and ConsoleExecutionHistory inline history render the same row contract with no second implementation
Full-output load/error/retry behavior and the post-load `toolRowPresentation` refresh (outputState 'full', stale truncated badge removed, disclosure state preserved) work identically in Console
packages/web/src/experiments/console/console-isolation.test.ts passes; it is modified ONLY if a shared-lib allowlist entry is genuinely required

After BOTH renderers consume item.presentation, remove the superseded context projection: delete `context` from the AgentHistoryItem tool arm, `TOOL_CONTEXT_KEYS` (:50), and `toolContext()` (:171) from agent-history.ts, plus only their tests — no other history behavior changes

All three rewritten HITL behavior cases pass end to end: `npx playwright test -c playwright.config.ts ui/workflow-run-hitl.spec.ts ui/workflow-run-hitl-room.spec.ts --grep "HITL.*readable tool row"` from e2e

Verification passes from packages/web: `NODE_ENV=development bun test src/experiments/console/components/ConsoleNodeRoom.test.tsx src/experiments/console/components/inspect/ConsoleExecutionHistory.test.tsx`, `bun test src/experiments/console/console-isolation.test.ts`, `bun test src/lib/agent-history.test.ts`, `bun run type-check`; no renderer contains resolver, headline, outcome, or badge-ordering policy
userStories.technicalNotes: Follow phase-02-two-surface-renderers.md implementation order steps 4-8. Console tool markup lives in ConsoleAgentHistoryList.tsx:156 (.ptool), :178 (item.context), :263/:277 (tool filter/render); this file serves both ConsoleNodeRoom.tsx and ConsoleExecutionHistory.tsx. Preserve Console boundary — shared lib data yes, Legacy component import no.

userStories.title: E2E visual verification, acceptance report, and full gates
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want deterministic geometry, focus, motion, and measured-width evidence plus a recorded human visual and screen-reader acceptance, so that Story 1.1 ships with proof rather than screenshot-only judgment.
acceptanceCriteria: e2e/ui/workflow-run-hitl-visual.spec.ts:117 readiness locator replaced with a visible direct-summary locator (`details[data-tool-id] > summary`) so it cannot pass on hidden descendant payload text; the older suite's capture ownership is otherwise untouched and HITL_TOOL_OUTPUT readiness dependence removed if unused

New e2e/ui/agent-tool-row-visual.spec.ts created with uppercase 'HITL' in its title (CI selector) reusing runHitlWorkflow/openRunDetail/openLegacyRunDetail, the existing inspect-node constant, and the stored successful tool fixture — no provider switches added to manufacture states

New spec asserts on BOTH surfaces: direct summary visible with readable chip/headline and closed row with output hidden; Enter/Space toggle with focus retained; a room-width helper measures 460 ± 2 px before every narrow assertion (splitter may be driven but measured DOM width is the proof); summary parts share one line and badges do not wrap at 460 px (DOM bounding boxes/tops, not screenshot-only)

Existing 1440/1024/768/390 viewport sweep and 200% zoom paths retained and assert the row stays operable and one-line wherever the room is visible, with no transcript-specific breakpoint and no page-level horizontal overflow

Computed-style assertions: focus outline 2 px opaque accent-bright with +2 px offset (Console) and −2 px (Legacy); chevron transition 120 ms normally and none under reduced-motion emulation; rest row has no inset fill/border, hover uses surface-hover; captures attached via testInfo.attach()/outputPath() with stable names

Mockup comparison at measured 460 px against the final mockups (key-transcript-states, key-console-node-room, key-legacy-node-room, full-transcript-review) using the repo's Playwright local-file precedent; the 520 px Console mock gets a test-only panel-width override asserted before capture; expected later-story differences (no Raw, no family bodies/diff/todo/task/occurrence, temporary Input/Output bridge, leaner badges) are recorded as expected, not failures

plans/260917-1011-issue-174-readable-tool-call-row/reports/visual-acceptance.md created recording the full measurement matrix (fonts 12/11/10.5 mono, transcript 10/12 padding, no adjacent card gap, summary 4/6 padding/8 gap/6 radius/≥24 px, chevron 9 px column + glyph 12 px column, chip 1 px border 1/7 padding 4 radius ≤24ch, body 2/0/8/29 margin + 2 px rail + 10 px padding, focus offsets, 460 px one-line behavior, viewport sweep, elision anatomy, chevron motion, contrast)

Contrast evidence: search/glob chip text and nonzero exit digits resolve ≥4.5:1 on both surfaces and applicable rest/hover backgrounds via component style assertion + browser token/color-mix calculation; focus outline ≥3:1; numeric ratios recorded; report distinguishes component-fixture evidence from real-fixture evidence and never claims a screenshot shows a state the fixture lacks

Five status treatments (succeeded/failed/running/interrupted/unknown) have production-markup evidence — real E2E for succeeded plus component suites (and history fold coverage for interrupted) asserting exact production class/style/token selection, not only text

Manual accessibility gate recorded in the report: one Windows pairing (e.g. current Chromium + NVDA) and one macOS pairing (Safari or Chromium + VoiceOver) with OS/browser/AT versions, closed/open announcement, whether expanded state is spoken, name order, Enter/Space behavior, pass/fail — a failed or unavailable pairing is recorded as a blocker, never silently waived

All gates pass from repo root: `bun --filter @archon/web test`, `bun --filter @archon/web type-check`, `bun run --cwd e2e typecheck`, `bun run validate`, and `bun run --cwd e2e test:ui:hitl`; plus from e2e: the three readable-tool-row specs and `ui/workflow-run-hitl-visual.spec.ts --grep "HITL"` and `ui/agent-tool-row-visual.spec.ts --grep "HITL"` — with no unrelated diff
userStories.technicalNotes: Follow phase-03-end-to-end-visual-verification.md in full. The report must separate Story 1.1-owned parity from named later-story differences; any other high-salience mismatch is fixed in its owning phase, not blessed as a delta. Do not move or rewrite the older whole-view visual suite.
